plain: Arcadia sits on an alluvial fan descending from the San Gabriel Mountains, with historic washes and high-quality groundwater.
notes: Substantially right; corrected in detail (con-04): the Raymond fault is a complete groundwater barrier only at its western end and much of Arcadia pumps the Main San Gabriel Basin.

plain: The current First Avenue construction is unusually precise ('laser level') and reads as a deliberate regularization of the street, not routine repaving.
notes: Corrected (con-12): the current project is arterial pavement rehabilitation plus pedestrian-safety concrete work, limits Huntington to Duarte (south of the core); the full utility/streetscape regularization of First happened in the earlier Downtown 2000 redevelopment era.

plain: Santa Anita Park dominates the town's land economy and crowd flows.
notes: The 214-acre track anchors the east side; city capital projects are funded substantially by track pari-mutuel revenue (Capital Outlay Fund, pl-r16).

plain: Local reference points rendered in the relay as 'Mary's' and 'René' (no further identifying detail).
notes: Not researched (coverage cov-13); identifying private venues or individuals is out of scope absent a public role.

plain: Lucky Baldwin once controlled the land, the water, the rail access, the townsite, and the gambling concessions simultaneously.
notes: Confirmed for 1903-1909 with one caveat (con-03): water control is documented as ranch endowment plus reported canyon rights, not a formal municipal water monopoly.

plain: The present Santa Anita Park (1934) is not Baldwin's original 1907 track.
notes: Confirmed (con-01): 1907 track stood at today's golf course site and was demolished; the 1934 track is a separate facility on a 214-acre parcel bought from Anita Baldwin.

plain: Santa Anita was used in 1942 as a wartime assembly center where Japanese Americans were incarcerated, then by the military.
notes: Confirmed (con-02): WCCA assembly center 1942-03-27 to 1942-10-27, peak 18,719; then Camp Santa Anita ordnance training to December 1944.

plain: A 1993 Downtown Revitalization Strategy and later plans reserved the station area and reshaped First Avenue/Huntington long before the train arrived in 2016.
notes: Unresolved (con-10): later public planning is documented, but the asserted 1993 title was not found in a nonexhaustive search of online records.

plain: Patient owners (Positive Investments / Rao Yalamanchili; Erik Wahl; Trammell Crow / Alexan) positioned themselves around the station area before and after opening.
notes: Unresolved (con-07): the retrieved 2024 purchase post-dates opening, while county deed chronology and pre-2016 ownership remain partially searched.

plain: A downtown improvement association ('DAIA') mediates between the city and property owners and runs on assessments.
notes: Confirmed (con-11) by an official City staff report documenting the property-owner-approved CBD, City membership on five parcels, assessment payments, bylaw allocations, and recurring in-kind support.

plain: The same professional intermediaries (attorneys, architects, engineers, consultants, brokers) recur across the downtown projects.
notes: Corrected (con-06): Studio One Eleven repeats within the two retrieved TCR project records. No cross-developer repeat surfaced in the bounded packet sample; agenda packets and the full project universe were not exhaustively mined.

plain: The city negotiated over municipal parking lots as part of parcel assembly.
notes: Unresolved (con-05): 2018 public-parking status is documented, but later disposition history was only partially searched.

plain: Feng shui / geomantic siting logic shapes what gets built and bought in Arcadia, given the town's Chinese-immigrant real-estate market.
notes: Corrected (con-09): one 2014 article reports feng-shui-informed siting in the mansion market; citywide causal influence and institutional-project application are not established.

plain: Ley-line / 'mana-sieve' imagery: the alluvial fan, the washes, the racetrack crowds, and the money flows form an energy-like system that the built environment harvests.
notes: Preserved as hypothesis hyp-02. Ley lines are a Western esoteric tradition (Watkins 1922/1925) distinct from the Chinese practices documented in this market.

plain: The 'laser level' precision of the First Avenue works suggests an orientation/alignment intent beyond engineering necessity.
notes: Preserved as hypothesis hyp-03; the documented scope (pavement rehab, bulb-outs) supplies an ordinary engineering explanation, and no orientation intent is documented.

plain: A single 'controlling man' might sit behind the formation; the author's candidate changed over the conversation (Baldwin, Strub, Kaufmann, Chandler, Stronach, Wahl, Rao were each tried in the role).
notes: Preserved as hypothesis hyp-04 and refused as an identity join (rejected-joins rj-03): the candidates occupy different, non-overlapping historical functions; among the documented layers in this reconstruction, Baldwin (1903-1909) alone held all of them concurrently.

plain: The author corrected earlier conflations between the 1907 and 1934 tracks during the conversation.
notes: The self-correction matches the documented record (con-01).

plain: The author walked back 'master plan' phrasing toward 'formation' language — the observed shape may be structural convergence rather than command.
notes: The walkback is consistent with the bounded comparisons in con-08: several core stages recur in sampled corridors with different actors, while incomplete control stages remain explicit.

plain: The street plan encodes a deliberate policy geometry involving First Avenue, Huntington Drive, and Valencia Way (with Foothill Boulevard as a frame).
notes: Unresolved (con-13): no such geometry appears on the inspected adopted-plan surfaces, but the plan universe was not exhaustively searched.
